note: Original places, batch 2 of 4: groves, orchards, gardens and growing grounds. Each is a Location under a wild or city, linked to the plants found there. Written for Asetheria; no third-party text.

entries.name: The Olive Terraces of Oros
entries.summary: Stone-walled terraces climbing the Oros slopes, planted with olives older than the League and tended by families who inherit the trees by name.
entries.body:
Terrace upon terrace of dry-stone walls climbing the Oros slopes, each planted with olive trees that have names, owners and a place in a will. The oldest are hollow shells that still bear fruit, and the harvest in autumn is a village event with songs, ladders and a feast at the press.

## What grows here

The terraces are the home of the [[Grey Olive]], and the wall-tops are lined with wild [[Juniper]] that the shepherds burn for its smoke.

## Visiting

A visitor is welcome at harvest and given a bowl of new oil with bread. The families will not sell a tree, but they will sell what it makes.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: one ancient tree is said to be older than the Titans' fall, and two families are suing over who owns it.

entries.name: The Cedar Stair
entries.summary: A stepped slope of black-green cedar on the high ridges, where carpenters from three empires come for timber that outlasts them.
entries.body:
A series of narrow shelves on the Cloudspine ridge, each crowded with dark, slow-growing cedars whose timber does not rot and does not warp. Loggers work the stair by rope and winch, and a felled trunk is lowered down the cliff on a cradle of green poles that is itself half a day's work.

## What grows here

The shelves hold [[Mountain Cedar]], and in the crevices above them grows the pale-flowered [[Mountain Spikenard]] that perfumers pay to have gathered.

## Visiting

The ridge forts will give a traveller a bed. A visitor who wants to climb the stair is told it is a bad idea, and is told again at the foot.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a cedar felled last spring had a sword-blade grown into its heart. It was an old Caerthain pattern.

entries.name: The Myrrh Wadi
entries.summary: A dry, thorny watercourse in the desert where the resin trees are cut by night and the gum is sold by weight against gold.
entries.body:
A dry watercourse winding through the desert, lined with low, thorny, grey-barked trees that weep tears of resin when they are cut. The collectors work at night to avoid the heat, nick the bark by lamplight and return at dawn for the hardened tears.

## What grows here

The trees are the [[Bitter Myrrh]] of the caravan trade, and a larger, scented relative, the [[Caravan Resin Tree]], grows on the wadi's upper bend.

## Visiting

A caravan master pays a toll to the resin-wardens and receives a seal. A trader without a seal is a smuggler by definition.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the wardens are watering the trees from a hidden well. A rival tribe has noticed and wants it.

entries.name: The Honey-Palm Oasis
entries.summary: A green pool in the desert ringed with tall date palms, a cotton field and a market for everyone who survived the crossing.
entries.body:
A deep spring in the red desert, ringed with tall palms whose fruit is the sweetest on the plateau. The oasis is a village, a market and a rest-house in one, and every caravan that crosses the waste stops here for three days to sleep, trade and bury whoever did not make it.

## What grows here

The oasis grows the [[Honey Palm]], a field of white [[Tree-Wool]], and, in the shade of the palms, a patch of the pale, sweet [[Sweet-Root]] that the children dig for.

## Visiting

The rest-house charges by the night and by the camel. The headman will tell a traveller where the next well is, for a price.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the spring has dropped a hand's breadth since the last caravan. The headman is hiding it from the market.

entries.name: The Fig Orchards
entries.summary: Sun-baked orchards above the strait where fig-growers hang wild branches in the trees to bring the wasps that ripen the crop.
entries.body:
Dry orchards on the sheltered slope above the Aeolus strait, where the fig-growers hang branches of wild figs in the cultivated trees each summer so that tiny wasps will carry pollen between them. The practice looks like superstition and works like a machine.

## What grows here

The slope is the home of the [[Wasp-Fig]], and the gum of the [[Weeping Mastic]] trees along the cliff edge is gathered by women in white head-cloths.

## Visiting

The orchard-keepers sell dried figs by the string and mastic by the pinch. A visitor is expected to taste before buying.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the wild-fig branches have been going missing. Someone is trying to ruin one family's harvest.

entries.name: The Pomegranate Walk
entries.summary: A long garden avenue of fruit trees and rose hedges, where the satrap's guests are served wine and bound by the seeds they eat.
entries.body:
A long avenue in the garden city, lined with pomegranate trees on one side and damask roses on the other, ending in a pavilion where the satrap entertains. The fruit is cut open at table and the guests are told that every seed eaten is a promise, and that the promise is remembered.

## What grows here

The walk is planted with the [[Blood Apple]] and with the [[Persian Damask]], whose petals are pressed for water in the city's copper stills.

## Visiting

The walk is open to the public in the mornings. The pavilion is open by invitation only.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a guest was found dead at the pavilion with his mouth full of seeds. The satrap says he choked.

entries.name: The Oracle's Vineyards
entries.summary: Terraced vines on the sanctuary's lower slopes, tended by temple slaves and harvested to a calendar the oracle sets.
entries.body:
Terraced vineyards on the lower slopes below the sanctuary, owned by the temple and worked by its dependents. The harvest begins on the day the oracle names, and a vintner who picks a day early or late loses the year's wine to the god.

## What grows here

The terraces are planted with the [[Wine-Vine]], and a stand of [[Thunder-Oak]] on the upper edge is held sacred, with its acorns reserved for the priests' swine.

## Visiting

Pilgrims buy the temple wine at the gate and are told it carries a blessing. The blessing is included in the price.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the oracle's calendar is changed by whoever bribes the priest of the vines. A rival house is in the habit of buying the date.

entries.name: The Covenant Garden
entries.summary: A shaded court in the oath-city where contracts are sworn under the oldest plane tree and the water-channels never run dry.
entries.body:
A square court in the oath-city, shaded by a single huge plane tree whose roots have been fed by a channel of clean water for six hundred years. Contracts of consequence are sworn here, under the branches, with the parties' hands in the channel. A bargain broken after such an oath is said to dry the offender's wells.

## What grows here

Besides the [[Plane of the Wells]], the court's beds hold fragrant [[Temple Hyssop]], cut by the oath-priests to purify the parties.

## Visiting

The garden is open to anyone with a lawful business. Swearing is charged by the hour and by the stake.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: someone has been poisoning the channel to void a contract. The oath-priests have not yet noticed.

entries.name: The Reed-Cutters' Fen
entries.summary: A maze of channels in the great marsh where punts glide through walls of reed and the water-lilies open each morning like blue lamps.
entries.body:
A web of narrow channels cut through the marsh by generations of reed-cutters, each channel just wide enough for a punt and marked by a knot of reed on a pole. The reeds rise twice a man's height, and the water between them is thick with blue lilies that open at dawn and close at noon.

## What grows here

The fen is the main source of [[River Reed]] for thatch, and of the fine, hollow [[Pen-Reed]] that scribes pay extra for. The blue [[Blue Water-Lotus]] is gathered for temples that burn its petals.

## Visiting

A guide is not optional. The channels change with the season, and the fen keeps what it takes.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a channel that was cut last year leads somewhere that is not on the cutters' map.

entries.name: The Salt-Cedar Shore
entries.summary: A feathery grey-green fringe along the inland sea, where the trees weep salt and the wrack smells of wormwood.
entries.body:
A broad belt of feathery, grey-green trees along the shore of the inland sea, their leaves crusted with salt they have drawn up from the soil and shed in a white drift. The wind carries a smell of wormwood and old brine, and the herders who winter here drink from salt-lined wells.

## What grows here

The belt is the home of the [[Salt-Cedar]], and in the sandy hollows behind it grows the bitter, silvery [[Sea-Wormwood]] used against worms and bad liquor.

## Visiting

The shore is empty of villages. A traveller who needs shelter is welcome at a herder's felt tent and will be given salty tea.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the sea has been falling by a hand's breadth a decade, and the trees mark the old shoreline. Something is visible beneath the new sand.

entries.name: The Almond Slope
entries.summary: A southern hillside that flowers white in midwinter, a month before anything else, and gives the sun-city its sign of spring.
entries.body:
A hillside above the sun-city planted with almond trees that flower in the depth of winter, a pale haze against the brown hill. The priests of the sun walk up on the first day of blossom and proclaim the end of the cold, whatever the weather, and the city holds a feast.

## What grows here

The slope grows the [[Early Almond]], and the herb-gatherers' paths along its upper edge are lined with silver-leaved [[Saviour's Sage]].

## Visiting

The slope is open all year. The week of blossom draws crowds, and the almond-sellers charge accordingly.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the almonds blossomed three weeks early this year. The sun-priests say it is an omen, and nobody agrees which.

entries.name: The Green-Nut Orchards
entries.summary: Dusty orchards on the plateau's edge where the pistachio crop is the satrapy's quiet fortune and the harvest is picked before dawn.
entries.body:
Long rows of low, grey-leaved trees on the plateau's edge, planted in dry ground and watered by qanat. The nuts split with a sound like a snapped twig, and the harvest is picked before dawn, when the shells are cool and the air is still. A good year buys the satrapy a new bridge.

## What grows here

The orchards grow the [[Green Nut]], and the fallow strips between the rows are sown with [[Old Emmer]], the old wheat that the orchard families will not give up.

## Visiting

A buyer should come at harvest. The families sell in the orchard and haggle in earnest.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the qanat that waters the east orchards has been blocked. A dead man was found in the shaft.

entries.name: The Umbrella Pines
entries.summary: A shaded coastal wood of flat-topped pines where pilgrims rest, lovers meet and the pine-nut gatherers climb with hooks.
entries.body:
A coastal wood of wide, flat-topped pines that make a green roof forty feet up, with open ground beneath them. Pilgrims on the road to the capital rest here, lovers meet here, and the pine-nut gatherers climb the trunks with long hooks and drop the cones in baskets.

## What grows here

The wood is the home of the [[Umbrella Pine]], and a hedge of fragrant [[Lovers' Myrtle]] runs along the road, said to have been planted by a goddess's gardener.

## Visiting

The wood is a free resting place. The innkeeper at its edge sells roast pine-nuts by the paper cone.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a courier's body was found under the third pine, and his satchel was empty. A myrtle sprig was tucked in his hand.

entries.name: The Laurel Court
entries.summary: A cloistered garden beside the games stadium where victors are crowned and the acanthus grows in carved profusion.
entries.body:
A cloistered garden beside the isthmus stadium where the victors of the games are crowned with laurel cut that morning by the priest. The garden's columns are capped with carved leaves, and living acanthus has been allowed to grow between them until the stone and the plant are hard to tell apart.

## What grows here

The court is kept for the [[Victor's Laurel]], and its borders for the spiny [[Bear's-Breeches]] that the masons copy on their capitals.

## Visiting

The court is open to the crowd after the games. During them, only victors, judges and the very rich get in.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: someone has been cutting the laurel at night and selling wreaths to men who did not win. The priest has noticed and is afraid to say.

entries.name: The Dyers' Fields
entries.summary: Red and yellow strips on the river flats where the city's cloth-makers grow their own colours and stain their hands for a living.
entries.body:
Long strips of cultivated ground on the river flats outside the mill-city, planted in alternate red and yellow by the dyers' guild. The fields are harvested by families whose hands are permanently stained, and the guild wears the colour like a badge.

## What grows here

The red strips are the [[Red-Root Madder]], dug and dried in the third year, and the yellow strips are the [[Yellow Weld]], pulled whole and bundled for the vats.

## Visiting

The fields are open and a visitor can watch the digging. The vats are behind a wall and a guild contract.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a guild member has been selling dyed cloth that fades after a month. Customers are beginning to talk.

entries.name: The Woad Pits
entries.summary: Foul-smelling pits in a forest clearing where leaves are fermented into blue, and the warriors who use it paint themselves for war.
entries.body:
A clearing in the forest dotted with shallow pits where woad leaves are crushed, fermented in urine and dried into blue cakes. The smell can be detected a mile off, and the dyers who work here are cheerful, tolerated and not invited to dinner.

## What grows here

The clearing is the main source of [[Warrior's Woad]], the blue the forest tribes paint on their skin before battle, and the same blue the Imperial dyers now use for the cloaks of the garrison.

## Visiting

The pit-masters trade with whoever has coin. They do not allow strangers to stay overnight.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the tribes have begun painting a new pattern. The pit-master says it is a war-sign.

entries.name: The Saffron Terraces
entries.summary: Lilac-carpeted terraces above the caravan city that flower for ten days a year and are picked by hand before the sun is up.
entries.body:
Terraced fields above the caravan city that are bare for fifty weeks and lilac for ten days, when the crocuses open together and have to be picked before the sun wilts them. Every household in the district goes out at dawn, and the threads are plucked at the kitchen table that night.

## What grows here

The terraces grow the [[Saffron Crocus]], worth more than its weight in silver, and the cheaper [[Poor Man's Saffron]] is grown in a lower field and sold, occasionally, as the real thing.

## Visiting

The ten days are a festival. A buyer who comes out of season finds the shops empty and the prices high.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a merchant has been adulterating his saffron with the poor man's kind and getting away with it. A competitor has the proof.

entries.name: The Garden of Quiet Death
entries.summary: A walled physic garden in the inland city where the state grows the plants it uses on its condemned, with a keeper who tends them gently.
entries.body:
A walled garden behind the magistrates' court, planted with the poison-plants the state uses for execution and the herbalists use for medicine. A single keeper tends it, a gentle old man with gloved hands, and the beds are labelled in tidy script: this one kills slowly, this one kills quickly, this one is a cure in a very small dose.

## What grows here

The garden grows [[Judge's Hemlock]], [[Stinking Nightshade]], [[Nightsbane]] and the pretty, deadly [[Beautiful Lady]]. A key to the gate is held by the chief magistrate.

## Visiting

A physician may visit with a magistrate's note. The keeper answers any question and offers none.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a bed has been disturbed. The keeper says he did not do it, and he has never lied before.

entries.name: The Dreamfields
entries.summary: Red-and-pink fields of poppy and autumn crocus on the plain, where the harvesters work in silence and are kept awake by shifts.
entries.body:
A stretch of the grassland plain turned over to poppies and autumn crocuses, scarlet in spring and mauve in autumn. The harvesters work in pairs, one cutting and one watching, because the fumes from the cut heads send a worker to sleep on his feet, and a sleeper in the field is a dead man by dusk.

## What grows here

The fields grow the [[Sleep-Poppy]] for the apothecaries and the [[Gout-Crocus]] for the physicians, who prescribe it in tiny doses for aching joints and bigger ones for the unwanted.

## Visiting

A stranger is not welcome in the fields at harvest. The villagers are polite about it.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the gangs are paid in poppy-milk. A man who tried to leave found he could not.

entries.name: The Hellebore Cliffs
entries.summary: A sea-wind-blown cliff of pale rock where physicians climb for the dark-rooted cure of madness and the mandrake that shrieks, they say, when pulled.
entries.body:
A pale limestone cliff above the sea, scoured by wind, where the dark-rooted hellebore grows in the cracks and the physicians of the League send a man with a rope each spring. They say the plant cures the mad and kills the sane, and the dose is whatever the physician is brave enough to give.

## What grows here

The cliff is the home of the [[Madness-Cure Hellebore]]. A cleft at the foot is sheltered enough to shelter [[Mandrake]] and [[Adder's-Tongue]], which the gatherers pull by tying a dog to the root.

## Visiting

The path is steep and the gatherers' guild admits climbers by examination. A guide is mandatory.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a climber has been found at the cliff's foot every spring for three years. Each held a hellebore root and had a smile.

entries.name: The Rye-Ghost Fields
entries.summary: A grain district on the plains where the barley feeds the legions and the black-eared rye feeds the dreams of the villages.
entries.body:
A broad district of grain farms on the Latium plains, laid out in strips and worked in the old way with oxen and wooden ploughs. The barley is for the legions, the emmer for the farmers, and the rye is for whoever gets the black-eared kind, which every few years brings a season of strange dreams to the villages that eat it.

## What grows here

The fields grow [[Legion Barley]], the ergot-prone [[Rye-Ghost]], and in the ditches and borders the useful weeds [[Soldier's Nettle]] and [[Hedge-Mallow]].

## Visiting

A traveller is offered bread. After a wet spring, the bread comes with a warning.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: in a bad rye year the village of the third furrow dances for three days and no one remembers. A tax-collector is due.

entries.name: The Truffle Flats
entries.summary: Pale, flat desert ground after a thunderstorm, where the nomad women dig for the desert's secret delicacy by smell.
entries.body:
A stretch of pale, flat ground in the desert that is dead for nine months and lively for three, when the winter thunderstorms bring the truffles up beneath the sand. The nomad women go out at dawn after a storm and read the cracks in the crust, kneeling to dig with a short knife.

## What grows here

The flats give the [[Sand-Truffle]], eaten raw with salt or roasted in embers, and sold in the oasis markets for a price that makes the women's trade sound like magic.

## Visiting

A visitor can join the digging for a fee and a tip. The women do not share the places they know.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a buyer from the capital has been bidding up the price. One woman has been followed home.

entries.name: Silphium Hollow
entries.summary: A sheltered fold in the plain where the last wild stand of a famous, nearly vanished herb is guarded by a family with a long memory.
entries.body:
A sheltered hollow in the plain, fenced and watched, where one family guards the last wild stand of a herb that once paid for cities. It is tall, coarse and ordinary-looking, and every attempt to cultivate it elsewhere has failed. The family sells a single stalk each year, to the highest bidder, in a sealed auction.

## What grows here

The hollow is the home of [[Silphium]]. The beds around it hold the bitter [[Bitterwort]] and golden [[Calendula]] the family uses as a decoy for thieves.

## Visiting

No stranger is let in. The auction is held at the gate, and the winner is blindfolded on the way out.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the plant is dying. The family has hidden the fact from their own children, and a rival house has noticed.

entries.name: The Ordeal Grove
entries.summary: A circle of grey trees beside the oath-city where the accused drink bark-water and the gods are asked to judge.
entries.body:
A circle of grey, gnarled trees beside the oath-city, within a low wall. Those accused of lies under the covenant may choose the ordeal: a cup of water in which the bark has soaked. The innocent are said to be sick and recover; the guilty are said to die. The priests hold that the gods decide, and the survivors hold that the dose does.

## What grows here

The grove is the home of the [[Ordeal Trees]], and a ring of tall [[King's Candle]] stalks marks the edge of the consecrated ground.

## Visiting

The grove is closed to the public except on ordeal days. The crowd on those days is large and quiet.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the priest of the grove can alter the dose. He has been selling verdicts.

entries.name: The Thorn-Rows
entries.summary: A tangle of choking vines and spiked hedges at the valley's heart, where the thorn grew inward and the plants have learned to hunt.
entries.body:
The oldest part of the thorn-brake, where forty years of unpruned growth have knit into a living wall. The vines here move in still air and the rows have the shape of a field that was planted and then forgotten. Nothing that enters is easy to find again.

## What grows here

The rows hold [[Assassin Vines]] that tighten on anything warm, creeping [[Creeping Kudzu]] that swallows the walls, and the bog-loving [[Moorroot]] along the damp northern edge.

## Visiting

The valley's wardens keep the road to the edge and no further. A fee is charged for a guide, and the guides are a quiet, scarred lot.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the brake grew inward after the massacre. At its heart, something is being fed.

entries.name: The Hedge of Healing
entries.summary: A cold-shaded hedge in the valley where the sun lingers forty minutes and the herbalists gather their salves.
entries.body:
A thick hedge along the valley's sunless side, planted generations ago by a physician and left to grow. The herbalists' guild trims it twice a year and gathers what it gives: bark, leaf, root and berry, all useful to the wounded, all slow to come.

## What grows here

The hedge holds [[Witch Hazel]] for bruises, [[Comfrey]] for bones, [[Woundwort]] for cuts and the red [[Heartberry]] that physicians use to quiet a racing pulse.

## Visiting

The guild sells salves from a stall by the gate, and the physician's lodge is open to the sick for a small donation.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a third of the hedge died overnight. The guild is blaming a rival, but the roots are rotting from below.

entries.name: The Mushroom Caverns
entries.summary: Damp, glowing caves under the forest floor where three kinds of fungus grow side by side: one that heals, one that does nothing, and one that kills.
entries.body:
A set of connected caves beneath the forest, damp and faintly lit by the fungi that grow on every wall. Foragers come here in groups of three, with a stranger's advice on what to touch: the three commonest species look nearly the same and are sorted by smell, by colour and, in the worst case, by trial.

## What grows here

The caves hold [[Embergill Bloom (Beneficial Mushroom)]], [[Nullcap (Neutral Mushroom)]], and [[Widow’s Bell (Harmful Mushroom)]], and the red-spotted [[Fly-Cap]] on the entrance ledge.

## Visiting

The foragers' lodge at the cave mouth keeps a book of the dead. It is large.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a forager returned with a basket of the harmful kind labelled as the beneficial. The lodge wants to know who relabelled it.

entries.name: The Mourning Cypress Walk
entries.summary: A black-green avenue through the dead capital where the dream-walkers once buried their kings under the trees that never shed.
entries.body:
A long avenue of tall, dark cypresses running through the ruined capital to the royal necropolis, planted by a dynasty that planned for its own funeral. The trees have outlived the dynasty and the city, and the avenue is still green while every house beside it is rubble.

## What grows here

The walk is lined with the [[Mourning Cypress]], and the burial-gardens at its end are planted with [[Vital Mauveroot]], which the dream-walkers claimed could keep the dead from decay.

## Visiting

The road to the walk is not patrolled. The few visitors who have walked it say it is silent, and that the shadows fall the wrong way.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the cypresses are all leaning the same direction, as though listening. At the avenue's end a door has been opened from below.
